The proposal aims to at least triple EU data-centre capacity within five to seven years. Its impact assessment estimates that EU27 installed capacity would reach 12.4 GW in 2025 while supply fell almost 3 GW short of estimated demand; its market figures rely on an external study that excludes private enterprise sites, including many dedicated HPC facilities. As of the 2026-11-02 check, Parliament listed the proposal as awaiting committee decision. These remain proposal terms and Commission estimates, not enacted policy or verified market-wide outcomes.

item.title: Latent Sparse Attention reports long-context attention speedups up to 10M tokens
item.description: A preprint introduces Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which clusters keys in a learned latent space so queries search cluster summaries rather than score every key. In author-run tests, its distilled form stayed near the tested model baselines at contexts up to 10M tokens and reduced attention-layer prefill and decode time substantially on two specific model families and H200/B300 hardware. The paper reports smaller end-to-end serving gains than the per-layer headline; its 100M-token result is an extrapolation. The linked implementation could not be accessed during this review, and no independent reproduction was performed.

item.title: Google and Oracle announce planned TPU capacity on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
item.description: Google Cloud and Oracle announced plans to deploy Google TPU capacity on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure starting in 2027. The Google Cloud Blog and Oracle press release describe OCI as the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs; Oracle says availability will ramp over multiple years, and its Chinese-language post describes a plan to reach gigawatt scale. This is a distinct announced supply route from Oracle’s NVIDIA accelerator expansion. The announcements establish the partnership and plans, not delivered capacity, customer adoption, OCI-specific TPU performance or economics.

item.title: Canada announces a staged equity investment of up to C$1.6 billion in Cohere
item.description: On Oct 29, 2026, Canada announced a planned commercial equity investment of up to C$1.6 billion in Cohere, to be made in stages alongside private investors. The government release says Cohere committed to at least 1,000 new Canadian technical jobs and C$1.7 billion in additional Canadian compute infrastructure by 2030. These are announced future terms; the release does not establish disbursement, completed hiring or delivered compute. A prior C$725 million Cohere/CoreWeave compute project is separately documented, and public records reviewed do not reconcile any overlap between the new job and compute commitments and Cohere’s Oct 30 aggregate plan.

item.title: Cohere reports a C$4 billion Canada investment and 1,500-plus job plan through 2031
item.description: In an Oct 30, 2026 company post, Cohere described an update to its Canada investment effort, which it said began in 2024. The company expects the multi-year effort to create more than 1,500 jobs and deliver more than C$4 billion in research-and-development and AI-infrastructure investment through 2031, including at least 1,000 technical roles. These are company projections, not independently verified spending or hiring outcomes. Cohere does not quantify how much is new against the existing effort. The government announced a separate staged equity investment on Oct 29; the public sources reviewed do not reconcile overlap between the plans or with the prior C$725 million compute project.

item.title: A paper argues that latent monitors must separate prompt-injection exposure from unsafe-action commitment
item.description: A paper reports that latent monitors trained on a mixed unsafe-versus-rest contrast can flag prompt-injection exposure without reliably predicting which exposed agent will take an unsafe tool action. In a generated-action AgentDojo grid, Qwen's naive contrast gives pre-action AUROC 0.556 for NLA text and 0.672 for an activation probe; training on exposed cases only raises the activation probe to 0.853, close to a matched visible-text TF-IDF baseline at 0.855. The paper reports related commitment-contrast results on Mistral-7B and OLMo-2-7B, but all three model families use AgentDojo and the generated-action study is not a live rollout.

item.title: China issues a recommended technical standard for large-model inference platforms
item.description: China's national standards catalogue records YD/T 7171—2026 as a recommended communications industry standard for large-model inference platforms, published on 2026-07-15 and effective from 2026-11-01. Its stated scope covers model compression, deployment, inference, platform services and management and provides functional reference for institutions using such platforms. The catalogue does not establish mandatory adoption, organization-level compliance or measured implementation outcomes.
